JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .40,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for death of Kum.M.Samyuktha, D/o.Maraka Venkata Raja Reddy in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 21.09.2021 at about 09.30 a.m., when deceased and her family members were proceeding in a car bearing Reg.No.AP- 02-BG-8997 at Haveri Bypass, NH 48 Road, Hanagal, Near Pole, Haveri while returning to Bengaluru, at that time, driver of said car driven the car in a rash and negligent manner and went towards left side of the service road and as a result, the car was turtled and she succumbed to the injuries and immediately she was shifted to Government Hospital, Haveri, wherein post mortem was conducted and thereafter body was handed over to the petitioners and they have spent .1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body,
funeral and obsequies and other incidental charges.

Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and was working as a Teacher in a private schools and conducting tuitions to the students and also preparing civil service exams and earning .25,000/- per month.
Due to untimely death of deceased, petitioners life have become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
The accident in question has occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-02-BG- 8997.
The respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. Insite of service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed his written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 has denied the contents of the claim petition specifically and categorically.
It has also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
It has also denied the place, time and manner of the accident.

Further contended that this respondent has issued certificate of Insurance under policy number 3100743573 in favour respondent No.1 to private car and the Sri.Maraka Venkatareddy vs Sri.C.Vijaya Bhaskar on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165043583/

Further as per charge sheet filed by police the driver/accused of insured vehicle has been charged U/s.279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC and Sec.3 R/w.181 of M.V.Act for not having driving license at the time of alleged accident.
Further the driver of insured vehicle alleged to have involved in alleged accident was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the same.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the daughter of petitioner No.1 and 2 namely M.Sowmya succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 21.09.2021 at about 9.30 a.m., Haveri Bypass, NH-48 Road, Hangal, Near Pole,
Haveri, while she was proceeding in a Car bearing Registration No.AP-02-BG-8997 along with family members, due to the rash and negligent driving of above said car and by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In the original petition the name of petitioner mentioned as M.Sowmya.
The petitioner filed an application u/o 6 Rule 17 of CPC for amendment of name of deceased.
The said application was allowed and amendment carried out by deleting the name M.Sowmya and inserted Samyuktha in the place of Sowmya.
In the issues name of the deceased shown as M.Sowmya and same was not corrected after amendment of petition.
Hence, at this juncture, it is required to recast the issue No.1.

Accordingly issue No.1 recasted as follows:-
Recasted Issue No.1 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the daughter of petitioner No.1 and 2 namely M.Samyuktha succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 21.09.2021 at about 9.30 a.m., Haveri Bypass, NH-48 Road, Hangal, Near Pole,
Haveri, while she was proceeding in a car bearing Registration No.AP-02-BG-8997 along with family members, due to the rash and negligent driving of above said car and by its driver?

On the other hand, the 2 nd respondent insurance company examined its Claims Service Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his side of evidence.

9. My answer to the above issues are as under:
Recasted Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1:- In this case the petitioners contend that on 21.09.2021 at about 9.30 a.m., at Haveri Bypass, NH 48 road, Hanagal, Near Pole, Haveri, the deceased Kum.Samyuktha had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-02-BG-8997 by its driver and she succumbed to the injuries.
11.
It is the case of petitioners that Kum.Samyuktha succumbed to the injuries in road traffic accident occurred on 21.09.2021 at about 9.30 a.m., while she was proceeding in a car.
The petitioner No.1 examined as PW.1 and produced Ex.P.1 and 2 FIR and first information.
The police have registered the case on the basis of complaint given by brother of petitioner by name Sri.Maraka Ashoka Kumar Reddy.

The complainant in his complaint he has stated that driver of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-02-BG-8997 drove the car in a rash and negligent manner, went towards left side of the service road and as a result the said car was turtle, as a result the accident occurred.
Ex.P.5 PM Certificate, wherein mentioned that deceased M.Samyukta died due to shock and hemorrhage skull injury femur fracture (left thigh).
After registering the case, the police went near place of accident and drew up spot panchnama and sketch at Ex.P.6 & 8, wherein the police have narrated the place of accident.
Further the petitioners also produced Ex.P.7 IMV Report, wherein mentioned that the damages caused to vehicle.

After investigation police have filed charge sheet marked at Ex.P.3,
against the driver of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-02-BG- 8997 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 & 304(A) of IPC, R/w.Sec.181 of M.V.Act.

In order to prove their contention, the respondent insurance company examined its Claims Service Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & 2 i.e., authorization letter and copy of insurance policy.
The respondents nothing placed before the tribunal to disprove the case of petitioner.
On perusal of photographs and sketch produced by the petitioner, it clearly shows that due to negligence on the part of driver of car the accident occurred.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.8, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.AP-02-BG-8997 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age,
avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love Sri.Maraka Venkatareddy vs Sri.C.Vijaya Bhaskar on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165043583/

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of the deceased Ms.Samyuktha is shown as 20 years.

The petitioners produced Ex.P.12 & 17 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card and SSLC Marks Card, wherein the date of birth is mentioned as 19.07.1999, the accident occurred on 21.09.2021, so the age of deceased was 22 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
In Pranay Sethi and others Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the age of the deceased is to be considered for applying multiplier.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme tribunal in Smt.Sarala Verma case "18"

(ii) The petitioners contended that deceased Kum.Samyuktha was working as a "Teacher and conducting tuitions and also preparing civil service exams" and earning .25,000/- per month.
In order to prove occupation and income of deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.
Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

In Pranaya Sethi and other Case the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was below 40 years.
Case on hand deceased was aged about 22 years.

In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court,
petitioners are entitled for additional 40% of salary to the established income.
The established income of the deceased was .15,000/- and 40% of .15,000/- is Rs.6,000/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .15,000/- + .6,000/- = .21,000/- per month.
Admittedly deceased Kum.M.Samyuktha was a spinster.

Hence as per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in above reported judgments 50% of income of the deceased is to be deducted towards her personal expenses and 50% is to be taken as dependency and it comes to .10,500/- p.m.

17. The respondent No.2 has contended that the driver of offending car was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

sentences.text:
"The summary of our findings to the various issues as raised in these petitions is as follows:
(i) Chapter XI of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 providing compulsory insurance of vehicles against third party risks is a social welfare legislation to extend relief by compensation to victims of accidents caused by use of motor vehicles.
The provisions of compulsory insurance coverage of all vehicles are with this paramount object and the provisions of the Act have to be so interpreted as to effectuate the said object.

(ii) An insurer is entitled to raise a defence in a claim petition filed under section 163(a) or Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, inter alia, in terms of Section 149(2) (a) (ii) of the said Act.

(iii) The breach of policy condition e.g. disqualification of the driver or invalid driving license of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2) (a) (ii) of Section 149, has to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

Mere absence, fake or invalid driving license or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to Sri.Maraka Venkatareddy vs Sri.C.Vijaya Bhaskar on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165043583/
8 drive at the relevant time.
( iv )

Insurance companies, however, with a view to avoid their liability must not only establish the available defence(s) raised in the said proceedings but must also establish "breach" on the part of the owner of the vehicle; the burden of proof where for would be on them.
( v) The court cannot lay down any criteria as to how the said burden would be discharged, in as much as the same would depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case.

(vi) Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving license is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach" to allow defences available to the insurer under Section 149(2) of the Act.
(vii) The question, as to whether the owner has taken reasonable care to find out as to whether the driving license produced by the driver a fake one or otherwise), does not fulfill the requirements of law or not will have to be determined in each case.
(viii) If a vehicle at the time of accident was driven by a person having a learner's license, the insurance companies would be liable to satisfy the decree.
(ix) The claims Tribunal constituted under Section 165 read with Section 168 is empowered to adjudicate all claims in respect of the accidents involving death or of bodily injury or damage to property of third party arising in use of motor vehicle.

The said power of the Tribunal is not restricted to decide the claims inter se between claimant or claimants on one side and insured,
insurer and driver on the other.

In the course of adjudicating the claim for compensation and to decide the availability of defence or defences to the insurer, the Tribunal has necessarily the power and jurisdiction to decide disputes inter se between the insurer and the insured.

The decision rendered on the claims and disputes inter se between the insurer and insured in the course of adjudication of claim for compensation by the claimants and the award made thereon is enforceable and executable in the same manner as provided in Section 174 of the Act for enforcement and execution of the award in favour of the claimants.

(x) Where on adjudication of the claim under the Act the Tribunal arrives at a conclusion that the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with the provisions of Section 149(2) read with sub-section (7), as interpreted by this court above, the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is Sri.Maraka Venkatareddy vs Sri.C.Vijaya Bhaskar on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165043583/
9 liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amounts which it has been compelled to pay to the third party under the award of the Tribunal.

Such determination of claim by the Tribunal will be enforceable and the money found due to the insurer from the insured will be recoverable on a certificate issued by the Tribunal to the Collector in the same manner under Section 174 of the Act as arrears of land revenue.

The certificate will be issued for the recovery as arrears of land revenue only if, as required by sub-section (3) of Section 168 of the Act the insured fails to deposit the amount awarded in favour of the insurer within thirty days from the date of announcement of the award by the Tribunal.

(xi) The provisions contained in sub-section(4) with the proviso thereunder and sub-section (5)
which are intended to cover specified contingencies mentioned therein to enable the insurer to recover the amount paid under the contract of insurance on behalf of the insured can be taken recourse to by the Tribunal and be extended to claims and defences of the insurer against the insured by relegating them to the remedy before regular court in cases where on given facts and circumstances adjudication of their claims inter se might delay the adjudication of the claims of the victims."

sentences.text:
With the above said observations, we answer the questions 1 & 2 which are referred for our consideration, in the following manner:
Questions referred:-
I) If it is shown the insurance policy is not 'Act' policy in terms of Sections 145 and 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, but a contractual policy issued collecting extra premium indicating insurance company has enlarged its liability, will not the insurance company be liable to pay and recover even it there is any breach by the insurer? II) In such cases, is not the rule to 'pay and recover' applicable in view of the mandate in Section 149, M.V.Act that upon issuance of policy, the insurer is bound to discharge the award as if it were a judgment debtor?

Answers:
i) The insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any conditions recognized under Section 149(2), even it it is a fundamental breach (that is breach of condition which is the cause for the accident)
and the insurer proves the said breach, in view of the mandate under Section 149(1)
of the Act.

But no such order can be passed against the insurer, if, on the facts and circumstances of a case, a finding is given by the court that the third party (injured or Sri.Maraka Venkatareddy vs Sri.C.Vijaya Bhaskar on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165043583/
10 deceased) had played any fraud or was in collusion with the insured, individually or collectively, for a wrongful gain to themselves or cause wrongful loss to the insurer.

ii) The court can also fasten the absolute liability on the insurer, if there is any breach of condition which is enumerated under Section 149(2) of the Act or any other condition of the policy if the Insurance Company has waived breach of any such condition or has taken the special responsibility to pay by collecting extra premium by covering any type of risk depending upon facts of each case.

iii) Before passing any order on the Insurance company to pay and recover, the Court has to examine the facts and circumstances of each case and if it finds that the victim,
injured or the deceased, in a particular case, was solely or jointly responsible for breach of such fundamental condition by playing fraud or in collusion with the insured, the court may exercise its discretion not to fasten the liability on the insurer.
iv) However, the court should not adopt the above guideline as a general rule in all cases, but only under peculiar facts and circumstances of each case and on giving appropriate reasons."

22. I have carefully perused the above reported judgments, with due respect to the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, case on hand, the driver of car did not possess driving license at the time of accident.
So, the ratio and dictum laid down in the above judgments are aptly applicable to the case on hand.
Accordingly, insurance company first satisfy award and recover the same from the owner of vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident and the driver of car did not possess valid and effective driving license.
Hence, insurance company first satisfy award and recover the same from respondent No.1 the owner of vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is allowed with cost.

The petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for compensation of .23,89,000/-/- (Rupees Twenty three lakhs eighty nine thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Respondent No.1 owner of Car is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award and he is at liberty to recover the same from the respondent No.1 owner of the Car.

17. The respondent No.2 has contended that the driver of offending car was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Further contended that the driver of insured vehicle who was driving at the time of accident had valid and effective driving license to drive the class of vehicle.
Except producing these documents, the petitioners have not examined her batch-mates to show that they are drawing salary.
18. The learned counsel for petitioner relied on citations reported in:
(i) AIR 2018 SC 2662 in between Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs Tata AIG General Insurance Co., Ltd., and Ors.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the absence of proper and cogent evidence, this tribunal cannot presume that she was drawing salary of Rs.25,000/-p.m as pleaded in the petition.
With due respect to Hon'ble Apex court, the facts and circumstances of above reported case and case on hand are not one and the same.
In the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal will consider notional income.
On perusal of all oral and documentary evidence placed both the parties, it shows that driver of car did not possess valid driving licence at the time of accident.
(ii) MFA 103438/2018 of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in between Smt.Renuka and another Vs Lakkappa and others Sri.Maraka Venkatareddy vs Sri.C.Vijaya Bhaskar on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165043583/
7 19.
20. In (2004) 3 Supreme Court Cases 297 between National Insurance Co., Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh and Others, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India at Para No.110 held as follows:-
Mere absence, fake or invalid driving license or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.
To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to Sri.Maraka Venkatareddy vs Sri.C.Vijaya Bhaskar on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165043583/
8 drive at the relevant time.
Insurance companies, however, with a view to avoid their liability must not only establish the available defence(s) raised in the said proceedings but must also establish "breach" on the part of the owner of the vehicle; the burden of proof where for would be on them.
( v) The court cannot lay down any criteria as to how the said burden would be discharged, in as much as the same would depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case.
(vi) Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving license is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach" to allow defences available to the insurer under Section 149(2) of the Act.
(vii) The question, as to whether the owner has taken reasonable care to find out as to whether the driving license produced by the driver a fake one or otherwise), does not fulfill the requirements of law or not will have to be determined in each case.
(viii) If a vehicle at the time of accident was driven by a person having a learner's license, the insurance companies would be liable to satisfy the decree.
(ix) The claims Tribunal constituted under Section 165 read with Section 168 is empowered to adjudicate all claims in respect of the accidents involving death or of bodily injury or damage to property of third party arising in use of motor vehicle.
The said power of the Tribunal is not restricted to decide the claims inter se between claimant or claimants on one side and insured,
insurer and driver on the other.
In the course of adjudicating the claim for compensation and to decide the availability of defence or defences to the insurer, the Tribunal has necessarily the power and jurisdiction to decide disputes inter se between the insurer and the insured.
Answers:
i) The insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any conditions recognized under Section 149(2), even it it is a fundamental breach (that is breach of condition which is the cause for the accident)
and the insurer proves the said breach, in view of the mandate under Section 149(1)
of the Act.
